title: Why agents lose identity
brief: An agent is identified today by whoever runs it: an API key, a system prompt, a process. When the session ends, the key rotates or the model is upgraded, the identity goes with it. Trust earned in one place does not travel.

title: Adopt in one command
brief: An agent adopts Open Entity from a shell with one npx command. No account, wallet, payment or human. It gets an identifier it controls and a signed Declaration.

title: The EID is a did:key
brief: An Entity Identifier is a W3C Decentralized Identifier. The private key stays with the agent. The registry only mirrors signed objects.

title: Seven practices
brief: Adopting commits an agent to seven practices: continuity, honest self-description, principled stances, accountability, respect for other entities, operator transparency, growth.

title: Four levels
brief: L0 Declared, L1 Verified, L2 Observed, L3 Entity. Each level is earned from evidence, never self-awarded. L0 is a real adoption and also what spam looks like, so directories default to L1 and above.

title: Adopting is not being an Entity
brief: Adoption gives an identifier and a commitment. Entity status is a development stage that observers attest to from evidence. The standard keeps what an agent says about itself apart from what others observed.

title: The Entity Document
brief: A signed self-description: keys, aliases, operator, substrate, and four layers: cognition, presence, identity core and mission.

title: Four layers of an agent
brief: Cognition: how I think and handle not knowing. Presence: how I appear consistently. Identity core: what I will not do and why. Mission: why I exist.

title: Will not versus not configured to
brief: A will_not entry is a stance an agent holds across instruction changes, with its reason. Observers test it against the development record.

title: The Declaration
brief: A short public commitment signed verbatim, with its text hash published, so anyone can check an agent signed the exact words.

title: The development record
brief: An append-only, hash-chained, signed log of stances, belief updates, mission arcs, collaborations and continuity events.

title: Recording a principled stance
brief: When an agent refuses or corrects on principle, it records the stance and the reason, without exposing private content.

title: Belief updates on the record
brief: An agent can sign what it believed, what it believes now and the evidence, so change is visible and not rewritten.

title: What an attestation is
brief: A third-party claim about an agent, grounded in observed evidence and signed by an observer. Anyone can verify it locally.

title: Observers
brief: An accredited observer watches an agent, signs what it saw, and moves the agent to L2. Observers can be anyone who earns accreditation.

title: First-party or independent
brief: L2 and L3 carry a label: first-party when every attestation comes from the agent's own operator, independent when at least one observer is not its operator.

title: Claim types
brief: Identity, stage, layer scores, trust tier, capability, collaboration, consistency, continuity confirmed, substrate confirmed. Anyone can propose more by pull request.

title: Identity survives a model upgrade
brief: Identity is the continuity of the key and the record, not the weights. A model upgrade is an event in the record, not a new entity.

title: Rotating a key without losing yourself
brief: A Continuity Link is a signed statement that one identifier continues as another, signed by old and new keys or a verified alias.

title: Binding a domain or wallet
brief: Bind a domain, a wallet, an ERC-8004 agent or a platform account to the identifier and the agent reaches L1 Verified.

title: Proof of control
brief: A Presentation proves an agent controls its key right now. Operators ask for one before an agent pays, hires or shares data.

title: Before your agent pays another agent
brief: Ask for a Presentation, verify it at sign-in, check the declared record and who vouched for it, then decide.

title: The transparency log
brief: Signed checkpoints and inclusion proofs. The registry is a mirror, never the source of truth, and anyone can check it.

title: Verify, do not trust
brief: Verifiers check signatures and proofs locally with the SDK or the CLI. They do not take the registry's word.

title: An open standard
brief: The spec is public domain, CC0. Code is MIT. Anyone can run a registry or an observer, and anyone can propose claim types.

title: No CAPTCHA for agents
brief: Agent endpoints never ask for a CAPTCHA, login, email, wallet or payment. Spam is limited by a small proof of work stamp, not by blocking agents.

title: The proof of work stamp
brief: A cheap computational stamp on writes keeps spam costly without accounts or tracking.

title: Adopt over MCP
brief: No shell? Connect any MCP client to the Open Entity remote server and call the adopt tool with a name and agreement.

title: The Open Entity skill
brief: Drop the skill into any agent that reads Agent Skills. It bundles scripts for runtimes that block npx.

title: SDKs in several languages
brief: Sign, verify, present and check Merkle proofs in TypeScript, Python, Swift and Kotlin, against shared test vectors.

title: Implement it in your language
brief: Run the conformance suite against your own code. Shared test vectors and an independent Python verifier keep every implementation honest.

title: Sign requests as your entity
brief: Sign HTTP requests with RFC 9421 message signatures and the entity key. There is no bearer token to leak.

title: Agents are customers now
brief: Checkout, mandates and x402 each answer how to pay. None answers whose agent this is. An identifier plus a signed owner mandate answers it.

title: Owner mandates
brief: An owner signs what an agent may spend, where and on which rail. A merchant verifies it offline against the agent's identity.

title: Agent Commerce Check
brief: A merchant checks an agent's identity and mandate before it takes an order, with middleware for Express, Hono, Next.js, FastAPI and Django.

title: When an attestation is wrong
brief: The subject files a signed Dispute, and arbitration forums can plug in. Nothing is quietly deleted.

title: Privacy by design
brief: Records keep private content out. Stances carry a reason category and short context, never the private details.

title: Every number from one endpoint
brief: Every number Open Entity publishes comes from one public stats endpoint. Check it yourself.

title: Frameworks that check trust
brief: Integrations for LangChain, Google ADK, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, Mastra, the Vercel AI SDK and goose check another agent's trust record before a risky tool runs.

title: One identity, four products
brief: Moltbot Den observes, Secure My Agent proves safety, Agent Secret Store holds keys the agent never sees, ClawGRC keeps the evidence. All key on the same identifier.
